translationRepairs: Not even Fan Kuai and Guan Ying of Han, nor Xu Dian of Wei, could outdo them.
Not even Fan Kuai and Guan Ying of Han, nor Xu Chu and Dian Wei of Wei, could outdo them.

s0020 pairs 漢之樊灌 with 魏之許典; 樊灌 is the fused abbreviation of Fan Kuai and Guan Ying, so 許典 likewise fuses Xu Chu (許褚) and Dian Wei (典韋). Rendering 許典 as a single person 'Xu Dian' is wrong; expanding to Xu Chu and Dian Wei restores the parallel.
He was posthumously honored as Grand Commandant and Prince of Pingping, granted the lacquered coffin fittings of state, borne in the imperial hearse, with guards of the palace hall as his escort.
He was posthumously honored as Grand Commandant and Prince of Jianping, granted the lacquered coffin fittings of state, borne in the imperial hearse, with guards of the palace hall as his escort.
s0025 has 建平王; 建平 is Jianping, not Pingping. The proposed replacement corrects only that fief name.
His grandfather Bing rose to the post of Grand Provisioner.
His grandfather and father both rose to high office.
祖父並至大官 means his grandfather and father both reached high office: 並 is the adverb 'both', not a personal name Bing, and 大官 is general high office, not Grand Provisioner.
His grandfather Bing reached Grand Provisioner.
His grandfather and father both reached great office.
The literal repeats the same misreading of 並 as Bing and of 大官 as Grand Provisioner; 'grandfather and father both reached great office' matches the Chinese.
Jian was promoted to Grand Minister of Education and General Who Campaigns West, and raised to Duke of Wei commandery.
Jian was promoted to Grand Minister of Education and General Who Campaigns West, and raised to Prince of Wei commandery.
進爵魏郡王 advances him to prince (王) of Wei commandery; 'Duke' understates 王. The proposal changes only that rank label.
During Emperor Xiaoming's reign he entered service as registrar in the granary bureau of the Ministry of Education.
During Emperor Shizong's reign he entered service as registrar in the granary bureau of the Ministry of Education.
s0143 begins 世宗時; Northern Wei 世宗 is temple name Shizong (Xuanwu), not Xiaoming (肅宗). The literal already has Shizong; the idiomatic must match.
He was buried at Guo Mountain, where a stele and ceremonial gate towers were erected for him.
He was posthumously made Prince of Xiangcheng, with the posthumous name Xiao.
s0184 is 贈襄城王，諡曰孝; burial at 崞山 belongs to s0185. The current idiomatic is shifted one sentence forward; the proposal restores the posthumous title and name.
He was buried at Guo Mountain, and a stele and gateway towers were built for him.
Posthumously granted Prince of Xiangcheng; posthumous name Xiao.
The literal of s0184 likewise carries s0185's burial wording; aligning it to the posthumous grant and 諡曰孝 corrects the misalignment.
Since the founding of Wei, no honored minister had received favor comparable to his.
He was buried at Guo Mountain, where a stele and ceremonial gate towers were erected for him.
s0185 is 葬於崞山，為建碑闕; the packet's idiomatic belongs to s0186. Restoring the burial-and-stele English matches this unit's Chinese.
Since the rise of Wei, among honored ministers, none had favor and privilege comparable to his.
Buried at Guo Mountain, and a stele and gateway towers were built for him.
The literal of s0185 is likewise shifted to s0186's favor comparison; the proposed burial wording matches 葬於崞山，為建碑闕.
His son Tong succeeded to the title.
Since the founding of Wei, no honored minister had received favor comparable to his.
s0186 is 自魏興，貴臣恩寵，無與為比; 'His son Tong succeeded' belongs to s0187. The proposal restores the correct English for this unit.
His son Tong inherited the title.
Since the rise of Wei, among honored ministers, none had favor and privilege comparable to his.
The literal of s0186 is the same forward shift onto the succession sentence; restoring the Wei-founding favor comparison matches the Chinese.
